description: Compose deny list (REVISED-PLAN 4.4, D27; v2 = W20a). ONE rule file for the portabase-recover CLI (jq + kit-tool), the dashboard engine (TS, src/fork/policy) and the agent (Rust, W17). Evaluated on the RENDERED `docker compose config --format json`; the raw YAML read-scope check runs first. Default refuse. `rules` are overridable per service only (typed ALLOW <svc>); `hard_refusals` never are. Signature and checksum failures are never overridable and are not policy inputs. Normative semantics: vault ADR-015; oracle: src/fork/policy/compose-policy-vectors.json.

rules.plain: wants full control of this machine (privileged mode)
wants to use this machine's network directly (host network)
wants to see and control every process on this machine (host PID namespace)
wants to share memory with every process on this machine (host IPC namespace)
wants direct access to hardware devices of this machine
wants extra Linux powers (capabilities) beyond the safe default set
wants full control of Docker on this machine (like a Traefik or Portainer would)

rules.directive: volumes: bind mount outside the restore folder
rules.plain: wants to read or write files outside the folder this recovery restores into
wants to share the network, processes or memory of another container on this machine

rules.directive: a Compose setting Portabase does not check
rules.plain: uses a Compose setting Portabase cannot check for safety

hard_refusals.plain: reads a file outside the folder this recovery restores into
uses a path Portabase cannot prove is safe (a variable, ~, .. or a relative part)
is not one valid Compose YAML document (syntax error, duplicate key or custom tag)
is too large or too deeply nested to check safely
refers to a Compose file Portabase could not read to check
has a service name with unexpected characters
has a top-level Compose section Portabase cannot check
is not shaped like a rendered Compose file

raw_read_scope.description: Checked on the RAW compose/override YAML BEFORE any rendering, recursively through included/extended files inside the root (depth <= 8, <= 64 files): every target must stay inside the restore root; $ or leading ~ = outside; include with project_directory is refused.
